metas.name: 1 Letter and 4 Digits (horizontal)
metas.note: 1 letter and 4 digits (horizontal) (X0000 / X-0000) This marking is only found in Tumbes and Piura and should always start with an A. (it is often accompanied by other regional markings like "6 Digits Vertical") Credit to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: 1S South of Ica
metas.note: The 1S south of the city of Ica is not divided and mostly follows the coast. The soil is often red or orange in these areas, and there is little-to-no vegetation. This road is also entirely covered with the Generation 4 camera.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: 2025 Copyright
metas.note: This will get updated and I will remove it/update the meta if it does. But currently (march 2025), 2025 copyright is only found here. (theres like one road in the north that has it also but looks nothing like this area) Ty to ritchie
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: 5m Poles
metas.note: Poles with 5m written on the bottom of them are only found in the north of the country. Especially in Tumbes, Piura and La Libertad. Credit to Peru poles doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: 6 Digits Vertical
metas.note: This one is common in the far north provinces of Tumbes and Piura, but can also be found in Lambayeque, Cajamarca and Tacna. It is usually paired with other regional markings. Credit to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: 7 Digits (vertical)
metas.note: This type of pole marking is most common in Cajamarca, La Libertad and Ancash. It can also be rarely spotted in Piura, Lambayeque and Tacna. Markings in the northern provinces can either have a solid black border, dashed black border or no border while in Tacna it will always be no border. Sometimes, instead of the first two digits there will be two letters (XX00000). If it starts with 2 or 4, it is Ancash. If it starts with 3, it is Cajamarca. 5, is La Liberdad. (Cred. to Pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: 8 Digits (vertical)
metas.note: When you see this one, it should be in La Libertad, although I was able to find one in Cajamarca and in Ancash. cred. to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Arequipa Vertical Sticker
metas.note:
A vertical white sticker with blue or red numbers places you in Arequipa Province.

Credit to wayfinder
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Arequipa Volcanoes
metas.note:
Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.

NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are only found in the southeast in the highlighted area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Banana Plants
metas.note: Similarly to sugar cane plants, banana plants are generally found in agricultural regions adjacent to the coast in the northern half of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Coastal Agricultural Valleys
metas.note:
Coastal agricultural valleys in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between dry mountains with no vegetation. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.

NOTE: Agricultural valleys in the north of Peru can look similar, but often feature more shrubs and trees on the mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Coconut Palms
metas.note: Coconut palms (and other species of tall palms) can sometimes be seen in coastal areas of Peru, mainly north of Lima. They are mainly found in the agricultural areas which are typically found around the major coastal cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Cusco
metas.note: The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both red brick and Spanish colonial style buildings. Cusco is surrounded by mountains on all sides and features an airport in the middle of the city. Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of La Paz.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Cusco sideways pole numbers
metas.note:
In the wider Cusco area and up to the tri-point with Brazil and Bolivia, concrete poles will sometimes have yellow stickers with black numbers going sideways.

Credit to wayfinder
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Divided 1N/1S
metas.note:
Highway 1N/S is divided in the highlighted area on the map.

NOTE: It is the only divided highway outside of cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Ensa/9 Digits (vertical)
metas.note: 9:This one is less useful as it’s quite rare but can be spotted in Lambayeque and rarely in Ancash. Similarly to the 7 digit version, sometimes there will be two letters instead of the first two digits (XX0000000). Ensa: Can be either in the form of a sticker: blue text on white background with black border or in a form of regular marking similar to company name markings. Useful for getting Lambayeque. Both are common on the same pole, which will place e you in Lambayeque. credit to pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Far North Peru
metas.note: Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often quite dry in appearance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Flat Desert Landscape
metas.note: Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Flat with Distant Mountains
metas.note:
A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Hell Road
metas.note:
East of Chimbote, there's a road where sundown and clouds conspired to create footage as if from the depths (or rather heights?) of hell.

Credit to wayfinder
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Ica Barcode
metas.note: Ica stickers look very similar to Tumbes/Piura stickers but the numbers below the barcode are significantly bigger and most of the time you should be able to read at least some of them. Rarely, Ica stickers can be spotted in Ucayali or Loreto. Cred to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Ica Yellow KV Stickers
metas.note: In the province of Ica, the stickers contain information about voltage (kV) just under the warning text. Here you can see some examples: Note that it only applies to this specific design with no additional text apart from the warning and voltage information. cred to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: ICASAC
metas.note: As the name would suggest, most common in Ica, although also findable in Ayacucho. cred to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Iquitos Vibe
metas.note: Iquitos is a city in northeast Peru. It is an isolated city with only Generation 3 Street View coverage. Three-wheeled tuk-tuks, overcast skies, and rolling Amazonian landscapes are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Juaja to Huancayo Valley
metas.note: The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: LDS
metas.note: LDS poles are unique to the Lima Province and Lima Region but they are way more common in Lima Province. Credit to Peru Pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Lichen
metas.note: Patches of light green lichen can be seen covering rocks and growing on the ground in high elevation areas of central and southern Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Lima Barcode
metas.note: This type of stickers can be spotted in both Lima Region and Lima Province. Unlike Tumbes/Piura and Ica stickers, Lima stickers have the numbers in the centre of the sticker and the barcode below them. Sometimes there is no barcode at all. The numbers are also even bigger than on the Ica stickers. cred to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Lima Boulevards
metas.note: Most of the boulevard-type streets in Peru are in the city of Lima. These boulevards are typically long, straight streets divided by concrete or a grassy berm.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Machu Picchu Car
metas.note: Within Peru, this white Street View car is found in central Cusco. It drives from the remote town of Aguas Calientes up to Machu Picchu.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Machu Picchu Trekker
metas.note: A trekker around Machu Pichu walks up a lot of stone stairs. There is lots of foliage, but you can often make out the iconic mountains and ruins.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Middle Lake
metas.note: North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally marshy and a range of mountains can be seen to the east of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees. I also mistitled the tag but I don't have the will to fix it right now.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Moquegua Bollard
metas.note: This cylindrical bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru. (It also only seems to appear on the 36A)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: North Lake Titicaca
metas.note: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Northern Roofs
metas.note: Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru. These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Northern Tuk-Tuks
metas.note:
Tuk-Tuks with open front compartments are primarily found in the northern half of Peru, and are especially common in northern Amazonian adjacent regions.

NOTE: This type of Tuk-Tuk can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Olive Tree Plantations
metas.note: Olive tree plantations can be found in the far southern region of Tacna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Pine Plantations
metas.note: Pine plantations are typically found in higher elevation areas of the country, away from the coastal deserts and Amazonian Regions. The most common types of pine trees planted are Pinus radiata and Pinus patula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Piura
metas.note: The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Pucallpa
metas.note:
The east-central Amazonian city of Pucallpa, which lies close to the Brazil border, has a consistent street grid of WSW to ENE. All of the coverage in the city was taken with the Generation 3 camera.

NOTE: Some northern and eastern areas of the city feature grids of different orientation.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Red Brick
metas.note:
s a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of red brick become more common. This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of western Bolivia, which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly. Additionally, buildings with blue tinted glass can be seen most commonly in the same areas.

NOTE: Red brick buildings can be seen anywhere in the country, so use other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Red Soil
metas.note: Dark red-tinted soil is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Rocky Outcroppings
metas.note:
In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, exposed rocky outcroppings are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.

NOTE: Exposed rocks can rarely be seen anywhere in the country, so use this meta with some caution.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Ruta 28B
metas.note: Ruta 28B between the towns of Kimbiri and Echarate is a paved road with very faded or missing road lines. It is also characterised by being a relatively small road with Generation 4 coverage, which hugs the hillside and is located next to a river valley.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Ruta 30C
metas.note: Ruta 30C in eastern Peru uses a white Street View car in Generation 3 between the cities of Planchon and Iñapari. It features dense forest, few villages, and resembles interior areas of Brazil. Some of this area has been overwritten with Generation 4. Most of this segment runs north to south. (Im pretty sure its basically all gen 4 now so idk how usefull the car meta is, but the road is still distinct)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Ruta 5N San Alejandro to Esperanza
metas.note: Ruta 5N between the towns of San Alejandro and Esperanza is a relatively straight, flat road in good condition. This road primarily runs north-south through the rainforest.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Sharp Mountain Tops
metas.note: Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: South Sticker
metas.note:
If you see a white sticker with blue text on a pole, you will be in the very south, below Arequipa

Creedit to wayfinder
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: South Titicaca
metas.note: Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of Lake Titicaca in eastern Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Sugar Cane
metas.note: Most of the sugar cane production is found in the northern coastal regions of Peru near the cities of Chiclayo and Trujillo. Typically you see large fields of sugar cane in these areas. Smaller areas of sugar cane can be found further south in other valleys close to the Pacific coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Tacna Ridge
metas.note: The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct dry ridge to the north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Tarapoto Area
metas.note: The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature moderately tall foliage-covered mountains and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of Colombia or Brazil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Train track
metas.note: A train track covered by a trekker is located between Aguas Calientes and Cusco.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Tumbes Offroads
metas.note:
These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either green or withered bushes.

NOTE: In addition, Tumbes does not have black cars on off roads. Make sure to consider it whenever you see such landscapes with a white Street View car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Tumbes/Piura barcode
metas.note: In these two provinces the main part of the sticker is the barcode. Under the barcode you can notice some numbers, but most often they will be too small to actually read them. This particular design can rarely appear in other provinces so use with care. Credit to Peru Pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: White Kv Sticker
metas.note: The letters on these stickers refer to the nearby city’s name. For example: JAE - Jaén. I have also found Kv stickers in Tumbes(extremely rare). Credit to Peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: With Support: Four Rectangles Poletop
metas.note: It only applies to this specific poletop with three horizontal bars and one vertical that resembles four rectangles. With a support bar is found in the South. The support together with the first horizontal bar can form a triangle or a trapezoid. cred to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Without Support: Four Rectangle Pole Top
metas.note: It only applies to this specific poletop with three horizontal bars and one vertical that resembles four rectangles. This Poletop without the support is only in the north. Cred to peru pole doc (desc)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.
